nodes.name: Cu foam cleaning
nodes.procedure: A piece of 1×3 cm² Cu foam was washed respectively with 1 M HCl, ethanol, and DI water for 10 min each to clean its surface.
nodes.source_text: In a typical procedure, a piece of 1 × 3 cm² Cu foam was washed respectively with 1 M HCl, ethanol, and DI water for 10 min each to clean its surface.

nodes.name: Cu(OH)2 NWA formation
nodes.procedure: The cleaned Cu foam was immersed in 30 ml aqueous solution containing 3 g NaOH and 0.68 g (NH4)2S2O8 for 20 min to obtain Cu(OH)2 NWA on the Cu skeleton.

unit_operations.name: Chemical oxidation
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: immersed in 30 ml aqueous solution containing 3 g NaOH and 0.68 g (NH4)2S2O8 for 20 min

nodes.source_text: Then, the Cu foam was immersed in 30 ml aqueous solution containing 3 g NaOH and 0.68 g (NH4)2S2O8 for 20 min to obtain Cu(OH)2 NWA on the Cu skeleton.

nodes.name: CuO NWA calcination
nodes.procedure: The synthesized Cu(OH)2 NWA was annealed in a muffle furnace at 200°C for 3 h to convert it into a CuO NWA.
nodes.source_text: The synthesized Cu(OH)2 NWA was annealed in a muffle furnace at 200°C for 3 h to convert it into a CuO NWA.

nodes.name: Ni(OH)x deposition
nodes.procedure: The CuO NWA was soaked in 0.1 M NiCl2·6H2O for 15, 30, and 45 min at open circuit potential to achieve varied surface coverage of hydroxide. After the deposition step, the electrode was rinsed with DI water thoroughly and dried at 60°C in an oven.

unit_operations.name: Ni(OH)x deposition
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: soaked in 0.1 M NiCl2·6H2O for 15, 30, and 45 min at open circuit potential

unit_operations.name: Rinsing and drying
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: rinsed with DI water thoroughly and dried at 60°C in an oven

nodes.source_text: Next, the CuO NWA was soaked in 0.1 M NiCl2·6H2O for 15, 30, and 45 min at open circuit potential... dried at 60°C in an oven.

nodes.name: CV prereduction to Ni(OH)x/Cu
nodes.procedure: A cyclic voltammetry prereduction process was performed in 1 M KOH with 0.1 M NO3- from 0.2 V to -0.3 V for 10 cycles with a scan rate of 5 mV s⁻¹ to fully reduce CuO to Cu while maintaining Ni(OH)x.
nodes.source_text: Finally, a cyclic voltammetry prereduction process was performed in the electrolyte from 0.2 V to -0.3 V for 10 cycles with a scan rate of 5 mV s⁻¹ to fully reduce CuO to Cu.

nodes.name: Ni(OH)2 solvothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: 0.7 g of Ni(NO3)2·6H2O was dissolved into 48 ml of ethanol under magnetic stirring, followed by adding 4.8 mL of oleylamine and 24 ml of ethanol in sequence. After being stirred for 30 min, the mixture was transferred to a 120 mL Teflon-lined stainless autoclave and heated to 190°C for 16 h. Finally, the precipitates were washed with cyclohexane, DI water, and ethanol thoroughly and dried at 60°C under vacuum.
nodes.source_text: Ni(OH)2 was synthesized via a solvothermal method... heated to 190°C for 16 h. Finally, the precipitates were washed... and dried at 60°C under vacuum.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images show Ni(OH)x/Cu NWA inherits micrometer-long nanowire morphology from CuO NWA, evenly distributed on Cu foam.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images show that Ni(OH)x/Cu NWA well inherit the micrometer-long nanowire morphology from the CuO NWA and is evenly distributed on the Cu foam skeleton (Fig. 1b and Supplementary Figs. 3, 4).

nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution TEM shows clear interface between amorphous Ni(OH)x layer and crystalline Cu phase with lattice spacing of 0.208 nm attributed to Cu(111) facet.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the high-resolution TEM image of Ni(OH)x/Cu, a clear interface is observed between an amorphous layer and a crystalline phase... A lattice spacing of 0.208 nm is recognized in the crystalline zone and attributed to the (111) facet of Cu.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM-EDS mapping shows homogeneous distribution of Cu, Ni, and O over Ni(OH)x/Cu nanowires and external coverage of nickel species on Cu surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Element mapping images indicate the homogeneous distribution of Cu, Ni, and O over porous Ni(OH)x/CuO and Ni(OH)x/Cu nanowires... HAADF-STEM combined with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy further manifests the external coverage of nickel species on the Cu surface.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman spectra of Ni(OH)x/CuO and Ni(OH)x/Cu show Cu oxide signals at 150, 218, 302, 630 cm⁻¹ vanish after CV prereduction; prolonged deposition shows Ni-OH at 457 cm⁻¹, Ni-O at 500 cm⁻¹, O-H at 3690 cm⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 1e, the Raman signals appeared at 150, 218, 302, and 630 cm⁻¹ which can be assigned as Cu oxides vanish after the CV prereduction process... The bands at 457 and 500 cm⁻¹ are attributable to lattice stretching modes of Ni-OH and Ni-O, respectively. The symmetric O-H stretching mode... at 3690 cm⁻¹.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns confirm Cu oxides reduction to metallic Cu in Ni(OH)x/Cu after CV prereduction; structure remains intact after long-term stability test.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Cu oxides reduction can be further confirmed by X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns (Supplementary Fig. 7)... SEM, XRD, and TEM results reveal that the structure and composition of Ni(OH)x/Cu remain intact after the long-term test.

nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution XPS: Ni 2p peaks at 855.9 eV (2p3/2), 873.4 eV (2p1/2) for Ni²⁺, satellites at 861.5/879.2 eV; O 1s at 531.5 eV for hydroxide; Cu 2p and Cu LMM confirm Cu oxide reduction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the high-resolution Ni 2p XPS spectra of Ni(OH)x/CuO and Ni(OH)x/Cu, two prominent peaks at bind energy of 855.9 and 873.4 eV... Cu 2p spectra, and Cu LMM Auger spectra over Ni(OH)x/CuO and Ni(OH)x/Cu electrodes.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge XANES shows very small edge shift compared to Ni(OH)₂ reference, indicating Ni valence slightly smaller than +2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ni(OH)x/Cu exhibits a very small edge shift in Ni K-edge X-ray absorption near edge structure (XANES) compared with the Ni(OH)₂ reference, indicating the valence state of Ni in Ni(OH)x/Cu is slightly smaller than +2.

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-EXAFS shows Ni-O peak at ~1.6 Å and Ni-Ni peak at ~2.7 Å; Ni-O distance 2.045±0.001 Å, Ni-Ni distance 3.113±0.001 Å, with reduced coordination numbers confirming disordered amorphous structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Fourier transform extended X-ray absorption fine structure (FT-EXAFS) spectrum and fitting results show the presence of two distinct peaks at ~1.6 and ~2.7 Å, attributable to Ni-O and Ni-Ni bonds... The nearest neighbor Ni-O and Ni-Ni bond distances of Ni(OH)x/Cu are 2.045±0.001 Å and 3.113±0.001 Å, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Selected area electron diffraction shows only polycrystalline Cu with no crystalline Ni(OH)₂ detection, confirming amorphous nickel species.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The selected area electron diffraction of Ni(OH)x/Cu only shows the polycrystalline nature of Cu without any detection of crystalline Ni(OH)₂, suggesting that the deposited nickel species exist in an amorphous structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-MS measured contents of Ni and Cu elements in Ni(OH)x/Cu samples.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The contents of Ni and Cu elements in the Ni(OH)x/Cu samples were measured on a NexION 350D inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometer (ICP-MS).
